business_problem: Cemex wanted to improve ball mill performance in cement production, a power-intensive stage traditionally controlled by human operators, to optimize product quality while reducing energy consumption and CO2 emissions.
solution_summary: Cemex implemented an in-house AI use case within its Digital Innovation in Motion ecosystem to optimize ball mill operations in cement manufacturing. The core method, called “Model-Based Optimization,” uses machine learning to build predictive models of mill performance from operating variables explicitly named in the story: the speed at which material is fed, separator speed, and main ventilator fan speeds. These models predict how the mill will perform and recommend settings that optimize characteristics affecting cement quality. Rather than fully replacing staff, the design keeps human operators in the loop to supervise and fine-tune the AI’s behavior. The source does not describe a storage tier or packaged vendor stack, but it clearly describes a compute layer where predictive models and high computing power are used to improve efficiency, product quality, and operational sustainability.

solution_components.name: Digital Innovation in Motion ecosystem
solution_components.role: Cemex's internal digital ecosystem under which the AI-based mill optimization initiative is deployed.

solution_components.name: Model-Based Optimization
solution_components.role: Uses machine learning models to predict mill performance and optimize variables that affect cement quality and energy use.

data_flow: Operating inputs from the cement mill process—material feed speed, separator speed, and main ventilator fan speeds—are fed into Model-Based Optimization machine learning models that predict mill performance. The resulting optimization guidance is then supervised and fine-tuned by human operators to improve cement quality and reduce energy consumption.
business_outcome: Cemex says the AI approach improves ball mill performance and can reduce energy consumed while producing a higher-quality product more efficiently, supporting lower operational carbon emissions.
